nodes.label: DICOM Domain Pack
nodes.rationale: Portable source of truth for DICOM and DICOMweb semantics.

nodes.label: DICOM Patient Study Series Instance Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Preserves clinical identity and interoperable DICOM data modeling.
nodes.norm_label: dicom patient study series instance hierarchy

nodes.label: DICOM UID Identity
nodes.rationale: Study, Series, and SOP Instance UIDs are immutable identities supplied by acquisition or archive; only genuinely new DICOM objects require a registered-root generator.

nodes.label: PatientID with IssuerOfPatientID
nodes.rationale: PatientID is only unique within its issuer domain.

nodes.label: Pixel Data Preservation
nodes.rationale: Avoid unnecessary re-encoding or lossy transcoding because diagnostic information can be irreversibly lost.

nodes.label: Domain Pack Wrappers
nodes.rationale: Agent definitions retain roles and boundaries while canonical domain knowledge remains in portable packs.

nodes.label: Incremental Graph Maintenance
nodes.rationale: Graphify hooks and a merge driver maintain the portable graph after changes.

nodes.label: In-Place Keycloak Realm Rename
nodes.rationale: Renaming preserves realm state and avoids duplicate import collisions caused by globally keyed literal UUIDs.

nodes.label: Shared Realm Audience
nodes.rationale: A single realm lets tokens issued for the BFF carry the Archive audience and preserve user attribution in DICOM audit trails.

nodes.label: OIDC Frontchannel Backchannel Split
nodes.rationale: The backend uses internal Keycloak HTTP for discovery and token exchange while browser-facing endpoints remain same-origin through Traefik.

nodes.label: Archive Internal-Only Access
nodes.rationale: The DCM4CHEE Archive must not be exposed to the browser; Quarkus accesses DICOMweb over the internal network.

nodes.label: Traefik Auth Router
nodes.rationale: Explicit priority 10 prevents the general SPA router from capturing /auth.

nodes.label: Docker API Proxy
nodes.rationale: Constrains Traefik Docker discovery to read-only version, events, and container inventory endpoints while rewriting unsupported API prefixes.
